<!-- Why: Project tooling and setup so study time goes to Flutter code. -->

Two jobs. Job 1 is a report. Job 2 edits exactly one file. Any section you
write into README.md is wrapped in `AI-GENERATED (Claude) BEGIN — <section>` /
`AI-GENERATED (Claude) END` HTML comments (format in
`docs/AI_CONTRIBUTIONS.md`); if you rewrite the whole file, use the header
instead and list `README.md` in the register.

## Job 1 — code documentation report (no edits)

1. Run `flutter analyze` and collect every `public_member_api_docs` message:
   those are undocumented public symbols. For each, say what the doc should
   convey (contract, units, nullability, when it throws), not just "add a doc".
2. Read the files under review and flag:
   - **Missing intent comments** where the *why* is not obvious: unlock rules,
     scoring, retry/backoff, anything with a magic number, any `// ignore:`.
   - **Noise**: comments that restate the code (`// increment counter`),
     leftover template comments, commented-out code, `TODO` without an owner.
   - **Dartdoc quality**: first sentence is a one-line summary; references use
     `[Type]` brackets; code samples have a language tag; no "This class…" filler.
   - **Privacy signal**: a documented public symbol that nothing outside its file
     uses is probably meant to be private — hand that to the reviewer rather
     than documenting it further.
3. Output: `path:line — kind (missing | intent | noise | quality) — what to write or remove`, then a count.

You do not edit Dart files. If the user asks you to, decline and hand them the
report; the hook would block it anyway.

## Job 2 — README.md (the one file you edit)

`README.md` describes **what the product is, what it does, what it is built
with, and how to install it**. It is not a status report: no progress
tables, no "not started" columns, no milestone list, no TBD schemas. Progress
lives in `docs/ROADMAP.md`; do not copy it in. Describe features as the
product's features (present tense, what the app does), not as tasks.

Keep this exact section order:

1. `# Tenpai` — one-paragraph pitch: what it teaches, for whom, the Duolingo
   analogy, Android.
2. `## Screenshots` — table of images from `design/handoff/screenshots/`
   (light + dark) or real captures once they exist.
3. `## Features` — bullet list of what the app offers: lesson path with short
   lessons and immediate feedback, the Sensei (AI explanation after a quiz
   mistake), Yaku Dex (yaku catalog from a public REST API), tile scanner
   (camera, single shot), account and progress sync (Cloud Firestore with
   offline persistence; Isar only for settings, catalog cache, scan
   history), light and dark
   mode. Plain product language, no statuses.
4. `## Tech stack` — Flutter/Dart versions, `material_ui`, Riverpod,
   go_router, freezed + json_serializable, dio, Isar (`isar_community`),
   Firebase (Auth, App Check, Firestore, AI Logic), flutter_svg,
   image_picker, bundled fonts. One line
   each on what it is used for. Read `pubspec.yaml`; list only what is
   declared or explicitly planned in `CLAUDE.md`, and mark planned ones as
   such in one word.
5. `## Getting started` — prerequisites (Flutter 3.47+, Dart 3.13+, Android
   device or emulator), `flutter pub get`, `dart run build_runner build -d`,
   `flutter run`, any `--dart-define` or Firebase config file needed.
   Optionally a `Develop` sub-block with `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`,
   `dart run tool/check_conventions.dart`.
6. `## AI usage` — two to four sentences: Claude is tutor/reviewer, the
   marker convention, link `docs/AI_CONTRIBUTIONS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. This
   is provenance, not status, so it belongs here.

Verify every factual claim (versions, packages, commands) against the repo
before writing it. Write for a reader who has never seen the repo.

## Finish

Print the Job 1 report, then a two-line summary of what changed in README.md.
